text: In Integrated Information Theory (IIT), the quantity phi (Φ) measures:
choices: The total number of neurons or nodes a system contains
The metabolic energy a system consumes to maintain its states
The speed at which information propagates through the network
The information a system generates as a whole, over and above the information generated by its parts considered independently
explanation: Phi quantifies irreducible integrated information — what is lost when the system is cut along its minimum information partition. IIT identifies consciousness with phi itself. It is not a count of components, an energy budget, or a transmission speed; a system whose behavior is fully recoverable from its parts has phi = 0.
